question: Can a separately verified host serial capture and derived telemetry bundle disagree on raw bytes or conceal a short host byte-arrival window?
baseline: Independent host-only verifier and raw-to-CSV bundle verifier; no combined chain/exposure gate
method: Verify both upstream contracts; compare byte-exact nonsymlink raw files and SHA-256; require >=600 s host duration, >=600 s first-to-last host byte exposure and >=600000 ms device telemetry span

provenance.input: Entirely fictional serial/firmware bytes and operator-declared host clocks; no device connection
provenance.runtime: GitHub Actions Python 3.13 ubuntu-latest/windows-latest; precise image digests TBD

results.local: 10/10 mocked-chain tests passed, 2 upstream integration tests skipped (modules unavailable in isolated copy); CPython 3.13.5
results.ubuntu: 75/75 full-suite tests passed, including 2 full-integration fictional tests
results.windows: 75/75 full-suite tests passed, including 2 full-integration fictional tests
negative_controls: host first-to-last byte span 0.5s despite declared host duration 630s rejected
derived bundle raw differs from host even with its own recomputed hash rejected
incomplete host, failed bundle, short device span, symlink and hash mismatch rejected

limitations: All data and clocks operator-controlled; coordinated forgery remains possible
Byte-arrival duration does not prove sensor sampling duration
No physical capture, calibration, independent review or deployment
decision: Keep stage; retain draft; no release
next_experiment: Issue #8 genuine >=600-second dual-sensor physical capture with independently inspectable setup, light perturbation and private raw-to-bundle evidence chain
kill_reframe: If physical provenance cannot be established, classify as logging tooling, not a sensor benchmark
